#3093. Sharplink (SBET) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Staking growth and a 72% ETH rally fueled a record quarter.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Sharplink, Inc. (SBET -1.76%) reported a transition toward internal treasury management and institutional Ethereum adoption following the termination of its external asset management agreements in May 2026. Management reported that the company is utilizing its permanent capital base to pursue long-duration on-chain yield opportunities, such as the Galaxy Sharplink On-Chain Yield Fund, which began deploying capital in late Q3. The company stated that its strategic focus remains on compounding ETH exposure per share through disciplined capital allocation, including opportunistic share repurchases and accretive financing. Management noted that the regulatory landscape in the United States is providing greater clarity for institutional participation through new SEC exemptions for tokenized securities and the upcoming implementation of the GENIUS Act stablecoin framework in Jan. 2027.

Operator: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for participating in today's conference call to discuss Sharplink's financial and operating results for the third quarter that ended September 30, 2026. By now, everyone should have access to the third quarter 2026 earnings press release, which was issued this morning at approximately 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time. The release is available in the Investor Relations section of Sharplink's website. This call will also be available for webcast replay on the Sharplink's website. [Operator Instructions] I will now hand the call over to Sharplink's Vice President of Business and Legal Affairs, Dodi Handy, for introductory comments.

Dodi Handy: Thank you, operator. Please see Sharplink's quarterly report on Form 10-Q filed this past Friday, November 6, 2026, with the SEC, along with the earnings press release that crossed the wire this morning at 8:30. These documents list some of the factors that may cause the results of Sharplink to differ materially from what we say today and identify some of the risks and uncertainties that could affect our business, prospects and future results. Sharplink assumes no duty and does not undertake to update any forward-looking statements. Any forward-looking statements made by us during this call is based only on information currently available to us and speaks only as of the date when it is made.

In addition, we may be discussing or providing certain metrics today such as ETH per share and other treasury-related performance metrics that are not GAAP measures. Please see our earnings press release and our SEC filings for further information regarding these metrics. To set the agenda for today's call, we will begin with Joe Lubin, Sharplink's Chairman of the Board, Co-Founder of Ethereum and Chairman and CEO of MetaMask. Joe will comment on key developments and emerging trends within the greater Ethereum ecosystem. Next, Sharplink's Chief Executive Officer, Joseph Chalom, will review our third quarter operating and strategic achievements, highlighting how we are translating Ethereum's growing institutional adoption into tangible opportunities for Sharplink and its stockholders.

Finally, our Chief Financial Officer, Bob DeLucia, will recap Sharplink's third quarter financial results, liquidity position and key ETH treasury performance metrics. So with that, I would now like to turn the call over to Sharplink's Chairman, Joe Lubin. Joe, the floor is yours.

Joseph Lubin: Thank you, Dodi, and good morning, everyone. Ethereum continues to evolve from a pioneering blockchain network into foundational infrastructure for an increasingly programmable global financial system. Its combination of security, credible neutrality, composability and next-generation trust infrastructure via rigorous decentralization provides shared financial infrastructure that institutions can build upon without relying on commercial intermediaries. Stablecoins, tokenized real-world assets and decentralized financial applications are increasingly operating on Ethereum, strengthening its already dominant network effects and expanding its role in the global economy. The scale of Ethereum's existing financial ecosystem, including Layer 2 networks, demonstrates its leadership.

Approximately $153 billion in stablecoin supply is supported by the broader Ethereum ecosystem, approximately $17 billion in tokenized real-world asset active AUM, representing approximately 55% of the tracked market, more than $58 billion in DeFi total value locked, representing approximately 65% of the global DeFi TVL, and approximately 1.8 million transactions per day on Ethereum mainnet, not counting the large amount of additional activity across its Layer 2 ecosystem. We believe Ethereum's 11-year track record of security, credible neutrality and reliable execution has established a foundation of trust that is particularly important for institutional adoption. Unlike proprietary financial networks controlled by individual intermediaries, Ethereum provides neutral infrastructure that competitive institutions can build upon with confidence.

Combined with its deep liquidity and extensive developer ecosystem, these characteristics reinforce Ethereum's position as foundational infrastructure for the next generation of global finance. One of the most significant developments during Q3 and subsequent to quarter end has been the continued acceleration of institutional adoption with some of the world's largest financial institutions deploying live financial applications directly on Ethereum. JPMorgan expanded JPM Coin, JPMD, its institutional deposit token, to Ethereum mainnet on October 19, complementing its existing deployment on the Base network. The bank specifically cited Ethereum's deep on-chain liquidity and established tokenized asset ecosystem as key reasons for the expansion, demonstrating how major financial institutions are moving beyond experimentation and increasingly utilizing Ethereum to support real-world financial activity.

Morgan Stanley expanded access to ETH through the July launch of its Ethereum Trust, MSSE, an exchange-traded investment product incorporating Ethereum staking as well as the rollout of direct currency trading on E*TRADE. Revolut, which serves more than 75 million customers globally, introduced phased testing of its euro-backed EURR stablecoin on Ethereum in August, demonstrating Ethereum's expanding role in programmable money and digital payments. ARK Invest announced the tokenization of its approximately $1.3 billion ARK Venture Fund on Ethereum in September, bringing a traditional investment strategy involving private and public growth companies onto blockchain infrastructure. Institutional adoption is also accelerating across other major financial platforms.

In August, BlackRock expanded its tokenization initiatives with the launch of Ethereum-based share classes for select European UCITS money market funds alongside 2 new U.S. tokenized money market products, BSTBL and BRSRV. Credit Agricole also introduced EURXT, a euro-denominated stablecoin issued on Ethereum. These developments demonstrate Ethereum's expanding role across institutional asset management, payments and financial market infrastructure with major financial institutions increasingly choosing Ethereum to support real-world financial applications. As more institutions bring assets, liquidity and financial activity on chain, we believe Ethereum's network effects will continue strengthening, reinforcing its position as foundational infrastructure for the next generation of global finance.

Alongside accelerating institutional adoption, Ethereum continues to advance its protocol road map to support significantly greater transaction volumes, improve efficiency and strengthen long-term resilience. Following the successful implementation of previous network upgrades, Ethereum continues to advance towards Glamsterdam, its next major protocol update. Glamsterdam is designed to improve Ethereum's ability to process more transactions in parallel and therefore, more efficiently while reducing reliance on trusted third parties outside the protocol that emerged to support the separation of the block proposer and block builder roles. These improvements reinforce one of Ethereum's greatest competitive advantages, its commitment to credible neutrality, decentralization and censorship resistance at scale.

Together, these initiatives reflect Ethereum's commitment to becoming the foundational infrastructure for global finance, delivering greater speed, capacity and efficiency without compromising the security, credible neutrality and decentralization that distinguish the network. We believe Ethereum's continued ability to evolve technologically while maintaining its core principles will be an important differentiator as institutional adoption accelerates. Ethereum's expanding institutional adoption and ongoing technological advancements strengthen our conviction in its long-term role as foundational infrastructure for the global digital economy. As financial activity increasingly moves on chain, ETH remains integral to securing the network, facilitating transactions and supporting the broader ecosystem of programmable financial applications.

Sharplink is strategically positioned to participate in Ethereum's next phase of growth through its actively managed ETH treasury, institutional expertise and commitment to supporting the ecosystem's continued development. Before I hand the call over to Joseph, I also want to briefly address the recent sale of Sharplink shares by Consensys Software Inc. While Consensys/MetaMask sold approximately 5.7 million common shares in October to better support its operating business, I want to emphasize that I did not sell any of my personal holdings. I have not sold any shares and continue to own over 5 million Sharplink shares personally, and Consensys and its affiliates retain significant additional equity interests in the company.

As one of Sharplink's largest shareholders and its Chairman, my conviction in our strategy and in the long-term Ethereum opportunity is as strong as ever. I'm fully committed to supporting Sharplink's continued growth and believe we are exceptionally well positioned to create meaningful long-term value for our shareholders. With that, I'd like to turn the call over to our Chief Executive Officer, Joseph Chalom, to discuss how Sharplink is translating this opportunity into disciplined execution and long-term shareholder value. Joseph?

Joseph Chalom: Thank you, Joe. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us. The third quarter represented an important turning point for the Ethereum ecosystem and Sharplink, highlighted by a meaningful recovery in the price of ETH, strong financial performance and continued execution of our long-term strategy. ETH appreciated approximately 72% during the third quarter, increasing from approximately $1,563 at the end of June to $2,681 as of September 30, 2026. Sharplink delivered double-digit revenue growth and materially higher net income compared to Q3 2025, benefiting from the appreciation of ETH and continued execution of our treasury strategy. The combination of growing staking revenue and a disciplined operating cost structure reinforces the operating leverage inherent in our treasury platform.

Beyond the financial results, Sharplink has made meaningful progress advancing several strategic initiatives designed to strengthen Ethereum's ecosystem, generate additional ETH and create long-term value for our shareholders. During the quarter, Sharplink continued to expand its leadership role within the Ethereum ecosystem, supporting initiatives designed to accelerate institutional adoption and strengthen the infrastructure underpinning Ethereum's next phase of growth. In addition to our previously announced support for EthLabs, Ethereum Institutional and EthSystems, we made a strategic equity investment in Blockspace, an Ethereum infrastructure company focused on validation and staking infrastructure. This investment further reinforces our commitment to supporting innovation and long-term growth across the Ethereum ecosystem.

Collectively, these organizations help establish the technological, institutional and operational foundations necessary for Ethereum to support a substantially larger share of global financial activity. Sharplink's involvement extends beyond providing financial support. It leverages our relationships, institutional expertise and broader ecosystem connectivity to support their development. Given our scale and position, Sharplink has an important opportunity to serve as a bridge between traditional finance and the Ethereum ecosystem, helping advance adoption while remaining focused on creating long-term value for our stockholders. Ultimately, our objective is to position Sharplink to benefit from Ethereum's expanding economic activity while identifying opportunities to grow ETH per share.

A central component of Sharplink's strategy is utilizing our ETH holdings as productive operating assets rather than simply maintaining passive exposure to Ethereum. A key advantage is our access to permanent capital, which enables us to pursue longer-term structured ETH deployments that may fit other investor mandates. Unlike capital that requires frequent withdrawals or rapid turnover, we can commit our ETH for multiyear periods, providing emerging on-chain protocols with the patient liquidity needed to establish and scale their operations. In return, we can negotiate differentiated economics designed to generate incremental ETH for our stockholders while supporting the development of the broader ecosystem.

We're focused on identifying these differentiated opportunities to deploy our treasury, generate additional ETH and enhance long-term stockholder value. During the quarter, we made meaningful progress activating several previously announced initiatives. In August, Sharplink announced a $200 million ETH allocation staked through Lido, further expanding our liquid staking capabilities. This deployment enables us to earn ETH staking rewards while maintaining flexibility to utilize tokenized staking positions across Ethereum's broader financial ecosystem. The allocation further diversifies our staking infrastructure and enhances our ability to evaluate additional on-chain opportunities, including using a portion of our Lido wrapped staked ETH as collateral to capitalize our Galaxy Sharplink On-Chain Yield Fund commitment.

In August, the Galaxy Sharplink On-Chain Yield Fund launched with $125 million of initial commitments, including $100 million from Sharplink and $25 million from Galaxy Digital. In Q3, the fund began deploying capital into on-chain investment opportunities, representing an important milestone in activating this strategy. We are in the beginning of a new phase we call On-Chain Finance 2.0. As more assets become tokenized, we expect RWA protocols to emerge to provide liquidity for trading and lending these assets. Additionally, new protocols continue to emerge as improved on-chain liquidity venues. However, these protocols will often have a cold start problem and need quality initial liquidity to ensure users have a good experience, enabling asset growth on their platforms.

By offering what we think of as jump-start capital out of the Galaxy Sharplink Fund, we can help solve this problem as more stablecoins and tokenized assets move on chain. This is part of how we want to put our ETH to work. Turning to broader capital allocation. Growing ETH per share continues to be our North Star, and we evaluate opportunities based on their ability to enhance stockholder value. As we disclosed on our last earnings call in June, Sharplink completed a $75 million registered direct financing at a premium to NAV with attached warrants, providing additional capital to acquire ETH and repurchase shares.

During the third quarter, Sharplink did not issue shares through its ATM program, reflecting our disciplined approach to raising capital and commitment to avoiding transactions that would dilute ETH exposure per share. We remain focused on maintaining flexibility across capital markets activities, including opportunistic financing, share repurchases and additional ETH acquisitions when market conditions support stockholder accretion. Our capital allocation decisions will continue to be guided by the economics of each opportunity and their potential to drive long-term value per share. Looking ahead, Sharplink is evaluating strategic opportunities across the digital asset ecosystem that could further expand our capabilities and take advantage of both our operating platform and permanent capital.

These could include operating businesses that address important industry needs, create additional sources of revenue or enable us to deploy our balance sheet better. We intend to remain selective, prioritizing opportunities that complement our ETH treasury strategy, meet our disciplined financial criteria and offer compelling potential for long-term stockholder value creation. The third quarter also brought meaningful developments across the global regulatory landscape, further supporting the institutional adoption of digital assets. While comprehensive market structure legislation in the United States remains unfinished following the Senate's failure to advance the CLARITY Act, we believe it's highly unlikely to be reintroduced given the results of last week's election.

That said, the SEC has advanced critical initiatives addressing tokenized securities, digital asset custody and pathways for broader institutional participation. Most notably, it has published an innovation exemption allowing for tokenization of U.S.-listed stocks and their trading on chain through SEC supervised venues built on public blockchains such as Ethereum. The SEC also proposed updating its transfer agency rules so that a blockchain can serve as a company's official record of stockholders. U.S. federal regulators continue its work in implementing the GENIUS Act stablecoin regulatory framework. On October 21, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued its final rule for the stablecoin issuers it oversees.

The rule sets clear standards for the reserves behind each stablecoin, how holders can redeem them and how issuers manage risk. The GENIUS Act and the OCC's rule both take effect on January 18, 2027, when payment stablecoins in the U.S. come under federal framework for the first time. That gives banks, payment companies and asset managers the clarity they need to issue and use stablecoins at scale. The CFTC has also continued efforts to provide greater clarity around oversight and the operation of digital asset markets. The CFTC has continued to open U.S. derivative markets to digital assets and tokenization.

On November 3, it cleared perpetual futures on individual stocks to trade for the first time on exchanges registered with both the CFTC and the SEC. That builds on its approval of the first crypto perpetual futures contract in May. The CFTC has also made it easier to use digital assets as collateral. We believe these U.S. developments are increasingly important for banks, asset managers and other financial institutions evaluating how to incorporate blockchain technology into their operations. Greater regulatory clarity can reduce uncertainty and help institutions move from exploring digital assets to implementing practical on-chain financial applications. Although there is additional work to complete, the direction of regulatory progress is encouraging.

Sharplink's strategy does not depend on any single legislative or regulatory outcome. We continue to operate within existing regulatory frameworks while positioning our business to benefit from the continued institutional adoption of Ethereum. Moving beyond the U.S. regulatory landscape, I recently participated in Korea Blockchain Week in South Korea and TOKEN2049 in Singapore, which reinforced the growing momentum behind institutional adoption of Ethereum and digital assets globally. Having visited Asia 5 times over the last year, I've witnessed a notable shift in the conversation from retail trading towards institutional adoption and real-world financial applications. Throughout my travels in Asia, there was a clear impetus to not fall behind the U.S. from a digital asset innovation perspective.

In each country I visited, the priority is establishing the necessary regulatory foundations, including for local denominated stablecoins, tokenized assets and trusted interoperable infrastructure and clear rules for market participants. I had the opportunity to engage with sophisticated financial institutions, regulators and policymakers, and it was encouraging to see the growing interest in Ethereum and its Layer 2 ecosystem as foundational infrastructure for this next phase of financial innovation. These observations reinforce our conviction that Ethereum's credibly neutral infrastructure is well positioned to support the next generation of global finance, further strengthening Sharplink's long-term investment thesis and commitment to advancing the ecosystem. We continue to believe Ethereum is uniquely positioned to benefit from the convergence of 4 transformative trends.

First, stablecoins are bringing programmable money on chain. Second, tokenization is enabling traditional financial assets to operate on blockchain infrastructure. Third, on-chain finance is creating new opportunities for assets to be traded, financed and utilized in continuously operating markets. And fourth, AI agents bring automation and continuous attention on behalf of individuals and institutions. We believe agentic finance represents one of the most compelling opportunities emerging at the intersection of artificial intelligence, blockchain technology and global financial services. We've seen meaningful progress in the adoption of AI agents and the development of the infrastructure needed to support autonomous financial activity.

AI agents are moving beyond simple information retrieval and becoming part of our everyday lives, helping consumers manage schedules, book travel, compare products and make purchases. On-chain activity is also beginning to demonstrate the potential scale of this emerging agentic economy. As an example, hundreds of millions of agent-to-agent transactions have been recorded through the x402 micropayment protocol, which enables AI agents to pay for services, such as data, computing power and access to AI models. These developments provide early evidence of a shift towards autonomous systems capable of executing transactions and managing financial activities on behalf of both individuals and institutions.

As financial activity becomes increasingly automated, these AI agents will require access to programmable money, tokenized assets, deep liquidity and interoperable financial applications. We believe Ethereum is particularly well positioned to support this infrastructure given its established ecosystem and ability to facilitate financial activity across competing institutions and applications. Building on this thesis, in September, Sharplink published research exploring the potential scale of agentic finance, including a long-term scenario in which approximately $4 trillion in annual financial services revenue could be reshaped by 2035. While the timing and scale of adoption remains uncertain, the research underscores the potentially significant economic opportunity emerging at the intersection of AI, blockchain technology and global finance.

These developments are laying the foundation of what could become a multiyear institutional adoption cycle for Ethereum. Ethereum's established liquidity, developer ecosystem, security and credibly neutral infrastructure position it as compelling infrastructure for a more open and interconnected financial system. Its ability to support interoperable applications and programmable financial transactions offers meaningful advantages as traditional finance increasingly moves on chain. Overall, Q3 represented a strong quarter for Sharplink, driven by Ether's price appreciation, growth in our staking revenue and continued execution of our strategic priorities. We expanded our ETH yield strategies, deepened our engagement across the Ethereum ecosystem and strengthened our position to capitalize on emerging opportunities in institutional on-chain finance.

Looking ahead, we're focused on 3 priorities: growing ETH exposure per share through disciplined stockholder accretive capital allocation, deploying our treasury into differentiated opportunities designed to generate additional ETH and enhance the value of our holdings and leveraging our institutional expertise, relationships and strategic positioning to participate in Ethereum's continued evolution as foundational global financial infrastructure. Our conviction in Ethereum's long-term potential is as strong as ever. As institutional adoption accelerates and an increasing share of global financial activity moves on chain, we believe Sharplink is uniquely positioned to capitalize on this transformation. By leveraging our institutional-grade treasury platform, strategic relationships and disciplined capital allocation, we can compound ETH per share and create sustainable long-term value for our stockholders.

Before I hand it over to Bob to take us through our Q3 financial results, I'd like to directly address the recent crypto exchange hacks. Sharplink has had no direct or indirect exposure to these incidents. Sharplink's crypto assets are stored with U.S.-based qualified custodians in hardware isolated systems, the same principle as cold storage. Incidents like these underscore the importance of continuously strengthening industry safeguards, reinforcing institutional-grade practices and building the trust necessary to support broader institutional adoption and on-chain finance. With that, I'll turn the call over to Bob for a more detailed review of our third quarter financial results.

Robert DeLucia: Thank you, Joseph. I'll begin by encouraging everyone to review our quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026, which we filed on Friday, November 6, 2026, with the SEC. The 10-Q provides detailed disclosures and footnotes that complement today's discussion, offering stockholders, analysts and investors a comprehensive view of Sharplink's financial position, liquidity and its treasury performance. We will now go through the financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. I'd like to remind everyone that all comparisons and variance commentary refer to the prior year quarter, unless otherwise specified. As of September 30, 2026, Sharplink held 602,361 native ETH with a net fair value of $1.6 billion.

In addition, we held 121,163 LsETH or liquid staked ETH, 66,379 weETH or wrapped ether.fi ETH and 57,393 of wstETH or Lido wrapped staked ETH with a combined net historical cost value of $482 million. Subsequent to quarter end, our combined ETH holdings have increased to 603,953 native ETH, 135,868 as-if redeemed LsETH, 73,601 as-if redeemed weETH and 81,695 as-if redeemed wstETH for a total of 895,117 ETH as of Monday, November 2, 2026. Total revenue for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was $13.5 million compared with $10.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase was driven by our staking and ETH yield generating strategies with staking revenue up 27% to $13.1 million.

We recorded a net realized gain of $75.2 million compared with a $6.3 million realized gain in the prior year quarter. The gain in the current quarter was primarily due to $55.6 million from LsETH redemptions, $18 million ETH staked for wstETH and $1.7 million from our contribution of wstETH to the Galaxy Sharplink On-Chain Yield Fund. We also recorded an unrealized gain of $676.7 million compared with a $107.3 million unrealized gain in Q3 of 2025. We also recorded an impairment charge of $1 million compared with a $7 million impairment charge in the prior year quarter. SG&A expenses in the third quarter were $11 million compared with $12 million in the prior year quarter.

The decrease reflects the elimination of $3.1 million in quarterly asset manager fees following the termination of our asset management agreements in May 2026. These decreases were partially offset by increases of $1 million in salary and benefits and $1.2 million in stock-based compensation, both primarily attributable to additional personnel hired after the third quarter of 2025 as we were building out our ETH treasury operating team. For the third quarter of 2026, we reported net income of $751.4 million compared to net income of $104.3 million in the prior year quarter.

The Q3 2026 results were primarily driven by the previously discussed unrealized fair value gain of $676.7 million and the $75.2 million of realized gains, which were offset by an impairment charge of $1 million. Overall, our third quarter performance reflects the recovery in ETH prices during the quarter from approximately $1,563 per ETH at June 30, 2026 to approximately $2,681 at September 30, 2026. As we've noted previously, the impairment charges and unrealized gains recorded this quarter reflect the current market pricing dynamics and are accounted for under U.S. GAAP. Just as in prior periods, impairment charges do not represent realized economic losses, and this quarter's unrealized gains do not represent actual realized economic gains.

Neither of these amounts change the number of ETH units we hold. Our treasury strategy continues to be evaluated on the disciplined ETH accumulation and the long-term productivities of those assets over time. As of September 30, 2026, cash on hand was $47.9 million compared to cash on hand of $28.5 million as of December 31, 2025. Between our cash position, our unencumbered ETH holdings and the flexibility of our capital allocation framework, we believe Sharplink maintains ample liquidity going forward to execute on its strategy across a range of market conditions and opportunities.

For additional details, our complete financial statements with accompanying footnotes, including all required disclosures and management's MD&A analysis are contained in the quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026, filed with the SEC. This concludes our prepared remarks. We will now open it up for questions from those participating on the call. Operator, back to you.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question is from Devin Ryan with Citizens JMP.

Devin Ryan: A question on kind of the progression of RWA on chain. And I know, Joseph, you talked about Sharplink being a potential investor in protocols to accelerate Ethereum adoption. Curious if you would ever look to potentially purchase some of these protocols or be kind of an acquirer of more infrastructure that connects to Ethereum, which would obviously bring in a different type of earnings stream, but potentially more recurring earnings stream and just how you guys are thinking about that over time to accelerate adoption. I guess just a broader question to just other things you're doing with capital to accelerate adoption. I'm not sure if I got cut off here.

Joseph Chalom: Devin, it's Joseph. Sorry, we were on mute. I think, we shared earlier this summer that tokenization and RWA is probably the most exciting use case that institutions are pursuing. And the majority of that activity is happening on Ethereum. And we're approaching it in 2 or 3 different ways. The first is the ecosystem investments -- the first is the ecosystem investments we've made in the Ethereum ecosystems with EthLabs, EthSystems and Ethereum Institutional. They are engaging with hundreds of financial institutions who are going to be the primary issuers and buyers of RWA. So that's number 1. Second is Ethereum is the leading blockchain for tokenization.

The last we checked over 50% of all tokenization issuance is happening in that ecosystem. But at the same time, we've shared with you that the Galaxy Sharplink Yield Fund is deploying into Ethereum ecosystem protocols. Some of them will be RWA oriented. The fund started making its first allocations to protocols in late Q3. And there are opportunities either to participate in RWA issuance ourselves by being buyers for yield or potentially to acquire these type of protocols. So I think we're taking a multifaceted approach. Nothing to announce on today's call.

Devin Ryan: Got it. And then as a follow-up, obviously, now Sharplink has native staking, several liquid staking relationships, the $200 million Lido allocation. We just talked about the Galaxy on-chain fund, strategic access through Consensys. So there's a bit of a portfolio here. And one question we get is you're trying to put this all together and quantify how much incremental ETH -- these activities could generate above kind of the native staking yield. I'm not sure if you can kind of give any sense of that or quantification just as we look out over the next 6 months to 12 months would be helpful.

Joseph Chalom: Sure. So the benchmark we use is the CESR rate. When you take a look back during Q3, the CESR rate performed at a 2.63% rate. And I'm pleased to share that we've again outperformed that benchmark in each of the months in Q3 and for the quarter overall, including rewards from our additional treasury deployments. We're not at this point yet quantifying the premium at this stage as several of our newer strategies, including the Galaxy Sharplink Fund are still in deployment and scaling mode. Our focus remains essentially on generating sustainable additive returns above traditional staking rates while maintaining disciplined risk management.

We do continue to believe even more strongly today that there's an opportunity to earn these additional returns above conventional staking through the institutional participation that we've mentioned in on-chain strategies. Again, it includes restaking, liquidity provisioning. Sometimes we receive protocol incentives because we have permanent and strategic capital for these emerging financial protocols. And so at this point, we're not disclosing the actual returns. Only that we've outperformed the CESR rate for the quarter.

Devin Ryan: Okay. I appreciate it. Is there any way to think about for the Galaxy fund, what the expected return? I know it's strategic as well, but if there's a kind of a targeted return on that capital?

Joseph Chalom: Sure. If you take a step back, the fund is designed to generate steady returns above traditional ETH staking. I would think of those as singles and doubles. We're not looking for triples or home runs here. Importantly, we are contributing our liquid staking tokens from Lido to capitalize the fund, which means we preserve the underlying staking yield while pursuing additional ETH-denominated returns through their selected on-chain opportunities. Again, our goal is to generate incremental ETH on a risk-adjusted basis.

And what I would share with you, Devin, is as the fund continues deploying capital and establishes more of a mid- to longer-term performance track record, we expect to be able to provide greater visibility into the incremental returns beyond conventional staking. At this point, there's only a handful of deployments, and we want to make sure we protect the confidentiality of each of those protocols.

Operator: Our next question is from Fedor Shabalin with B. Riley Securities.

Fedor Shabalin: I did have a question on the Blockspace investment. Sorry if I missed that, but can you size this investment and walk us through the rationale behind this? Specifically, does it kind of lower your validator or custody cost or maybe improve staking yield or give some economics in Blockspace's broader client base. Should we kind of think of it as one-off ecosystem investment or kind of start of vertical integration strategy in staking infrastructure?

Joseph Chalom: Thank you, Fedor. So the way to think about Blockspace, which is a sub-$0.5 million equity investment, it reflects kind of the broader commitment we have at Sharplink to supporting emerging infrastructure that underpins Ethereum's long-term growth. Blockspace, in particular, is focused on a few critical areas of Ethereum's infrastructure. It includes block building, validation and staking. Each of these are fundamental to the network's security, efficiency and continued development. We view our Blockspace equity investment as a strategic investment that complements our core ETH treasury strategy.

We are going to be in the business as we've been very vocal in supporting companies that are developing important Ethereum infrastructure because we believe we're both stewards and investors that can help strengthen the ecosystem while potentially participating in the economic value created as more and more institutional adoption and on-chain activity expands. Again, our North Star and priority is growing ETH per share, and we're going to do that through disciplined capital allocation and treasury management.

And the investments in private companies, including the one we made in Blockspace provide us not only an ability to fund the ecosystem, but also an additional opportunity to support that objective while maintaining our exposure to the long-term growth of the Ethereum ecosystem. So you can think of it less as a vertical integration play, but helping support really important infrastructure with potential economic upside as an equity investor.

Fedor Shabalin: And if you allow the follow-up, it's my follow-up, kind of follow up on Devin's question on Ethereum adoption overall. You know that accelerating institutional adoption positions Sharplink to grow ETH per share. But maybe which adoption milestones near term do you see as most consequential for Ethereum price? Maybe if you can, maybe it's a good time to rehash the -- like this theoretical equation, which variables should move and how much Ethereum in theory should respond, just like a pure quantification question, if it makes sense.

Joseph Chalom: It does. So I think in the short term, you should think of the 2 most important being the growth of stablecoin circulation and the growth of tokenized assets. Both of those primitives are dominated on the Ethereum ecosystem. Over 50% of all stablecoin circulation and transaction is on Ethereum. The same is true on tokenization. I personally believe tokenization is where most of the highest value activity is going to start from, and then it's going to happen on chain. And so DeFi and On-Chain activity was built on Ethereum. It has the predominance of that activity.

And as you start combining stablecoins as the money layer, tokenization as the asset exposure layer and third, on-chain execution, I think you'll end up seeing a lot more activity by more and more institutional users. In the longer run, I believe agentic finance will help automate and continuously execute these transactions. But I think in the immediate term, it's mostly going to be stablecoins, tokenized assets on DeFi and on-chain activity. For most of its history, Ethereum has been building and doing the hard work, which is ensuring it has the security, the neutrality, the censorship resistance, that distinguishes it from every other blockchain around.

I think you're now going to see the phase of more and more transaction activity. The newest releases coming from Ethereum will significantly reduce costs and increase speeds, and that will inure to the Ethereum price. I also think Ethereum is a store of value, and it's starting to get more and more attention in that regard. So I think the short term, stablecoins, tokenization and on-chain activity in the longer term, it's going to be agentic transactions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our next question is from Kevin Dede with JonesTrading.

Kevin Dede: I just cursory analysis here, but it looked like native staking fees increased sequentially. And I was wondering if you might address that.

Joseph Chalom: So the native Ethereum staking is driven by supply-demand dynamics and the actual yield is dynamic in nature. We've seen periods where it was around 3%. We've also seen periods recently where it was around 2.5%. Right now, if you look back over the last quarter, it's been averaging a little bit closer to 2.65%, but that will change over time. We're less concerned with the actual yield. We're more concerned and focused on making sure that we're deploying our entire balance sheet, and we're doing it in a way that's safe and disciplined. And again, over time, because we have permanent capital, we can outperform the Ethereum staking rate.

We've done that for the last several quarters, and we anticipate being able to share more detail on that as our newest deployments go into production, including the Galaxy Sharplink Yield Fund. But it is based on supply and demand dynamics. We saw a period over the last 1.5 years since ETF started staking and more importantly, the digital asset treasury started staking where the percentage of staking rates on Ethereum is now north of 35%, and that will drive both the yield you receive as well as the queue and unqueue time for staking your ETH.

Kevin Dede: I apologize, Joseph, I think I misframed my question. I was more curious about the validator fees, in fact, that Sharplink is paying. It looked like they were up almost 100 basis points sequentially. And I was wondering how you think we should think about that. I understand the fluidity in ETH staking returns. Just not sure about in light of Fedor's question, too, right, with your Blockspace investments, how you plan on managing native staking?

Joseph Chalom: Sure. Most of our native staking is done on a delegated basis, Kevin, through both Coinbase and Anchorage. And we pay them a fixed percentage of our staking rewards, single digit, low single digits. I can't go into the details for confidentiality. But the amount of absolute fees we share on both custody and staking rewards will depend on the total AUM that's being staked. And as we acquire more ETH or the price of ETH goes up, we will pay more custody fees, we will receive more rewards, and we will pay more rewards in sharing with our validators. But that's managed primarily through our relationships with Anchorage Digital and Coinbase.

It's a fixed percentage of our ETH rewards being received, but we'll receive more rewards as the price of ETH expands.

Kevin Dede: KPMG as your auditors, how much oversight will they actually have over the Galaxy fund and the Linea DeFi activity? Just kind of curious about how auditors are going to resolve the intricacies of decentralized finance.

Joseph Chalom: Sure. I mean, the auditors are involved in auditing and classifying the income and revenue from every deployment we make, whether it's the Linea, ether.fi, Eigen, Lido deployments, they're actively involved. They are independent auditors, and they focus on GAAP standards and issue opinions and audit our financials. With respect to the Galaxy fund, the fund has its own auditors. Galaxy as the manager of the fund publishes accounting and NAV reports. But then how it's classified is -- how the returns are classified is handled by KPMG as our external auditor. I don't think there's anything more to share. We work very closely with them, and we rely on them to help audit our financials.

Kevin Pimental: This is Kevin on for Brian. Are you having discussions with Galaxy or others about other funds where you can deploy capital?

Joseph Chalom: Just taking a step back, when we started our strategy in June of 2025, we didn't have in-house capabilities to do full asset management. So we had engaged initially on a nonexclusive basis, 2 asset managers to help us on our ETH purchases and staking. As we disclosed in May, for the basic asset management capabilities, we've terminated those external relationships. But when we try to do on-chain deployments in scale, we engaged Galaxy in this fund together, where together, we've allocated 100 -- sorry, we've committed $125 million of assets.

Galaxy has unique capabilities to not only source these opportunities, but to deploy and monitor them in scale. That's why in this high value-add engagement, we did it through a fund structure. Kevin, I would tell you, on a weekly basis, we're meeting with protocols, DeFi providers, fund managers to explore opportunities, but we haven't announced anything new. So right now, many of the initial deployments are done in-house. We do our staking oversight in-house, but we have this one fund structure with Galaxy to do on-chain yield and to do it in scale.

Kevin Pimental: Great. And then just a second one. How important do you view Glamsterdam to Ethereum's investment thesis? And are you seeing any developments from the upgrade that could materially improve Ethereum's economics or the institutional adoption?

Joseph Chalom: Joe Lubin, I'll turn this one over to you.

Joseph Lubin: Sure. Thank you. So Glamsterdam is certainly important to the evolution of the Ethereum platform. In terms of institutional adoption, I think it's relatively immaterial. It certainly does provide some benefits in reducing our reliance on centralization in the proposer-builder separation construct. It will increase throughput. It is adjusting pricing. But the institutions are coming anyway. And I think from what we're seeing, institutional adoption is effectively independent of the advancements of Glamsterdam.

Operator: Our next question is from Joseph Vafi with Canaccord Genuity.

Joseph Vafi: Nice progress on a bunch of fronts. I was just wondering at a high level, if we think about GENIUS Act being fully implemented here early in the year, along with some of the RWA, how do you see it kind of maybe at a high level, how that may ultimately move spot, how there may be a bit of a decoupling effect from other correlated assets and how those trends help the underlying native staking yield? And then I have a quick follow-up.

Joseph Chalom: Sure. When I think about the CLARITY Act, which didn't pass cloture in the Senate, we were actually quite happy with what the SEC and CFTC have done since. The 2 most important green lights we have for institutions are GENIUS. And I had mentioned in my opening remarks, the OCC guidance around stablecoins and the fact that the GENIUS Act will take effect in January of 2027. That will unlock the world's largest institutions to start participating in stablecoins. The second is the SEC's innovation exemption, which is providing a 5-year ramp and clarity to tokenization to allow certain venues that are not necessarily national stock exchanges to do automated market making and support U.S. equity tokenization.

We're going to start seeing that on NASDAQ, New York Stock Exchange, but we're also seeing important developments on the DTCC front, the ability to dematerialize collateral in accounts and allow them to be tokenized so that members can move them from one account to another in a very, very rapid intraday manner. What both of these things are going to do is stimulate stablecoin circulation and use cases as well as tokenization of U.S. equities. And when those 2 things happen, we believe the activity over 50% historically will happen in the Ethereum ecosystem. We'll see more users come online. We'll see institutions go from experimentation to production.

And then the interesting element is when you have these tokenized assets for the first time, we have an ability to see them borrowed against, lent against on chain, whether you call it DeFi or on-chain 2.0, that's where you're going to see a lot of the composability. And we see Ethereum being at the forefront of that activity, and it's going to benefit the price of Ether. I won't make short-term price predictions, but this is the exact thesis we've been talking about since last June, and we're seeing it play out live in real time.

And we're quite encouraged by the fact that the SEC, CFTC and OCC are providing the guidance needed for the world's largest institutions to come on chain. While it's starting in the U.S., we're very encouraged by what we're seeing in Asia as well.

Joseph Vafi: Great color, Joseph. And then quickly on the registered direct during the quarter. Obviously, you have a lot of liquidity with your balance, and I understand it was accretive to ETH per share. Just -- maybe just a few extra thoughts on kind of the strategic use here of the registered direct in the quarter.

Joseph Chalom: Sure. I think we've said publicly that when our multiple to NAV is below 1, we are not in the business of raising capital through the ATM because it could be dilutive for shareholders. We used the ATM last year when it was accretive to shareholders. But the interesting thing about running an Ethereum treasury company is we have every day the flexibility across multiple investment opportunities. Obviously, we own ETH directly, and that gives our clients and our investors an opportunity to get the capital appreciation. But when we think of disciplined capital allocation, we are opportunistic. There are moments where it doesn't make sense to raise. I would tell you it's very sentiment oriented.

When the price of ETH in Q3 expanded, the number of calls coming in from institutions, whether they were hedge funds or banks, interested in buying our shares through registered directs increased, but we're going to be very, very careful. And where it makes sense, we've done it twice. We will do the premium to NAV financing. At the same time, you've seen our cash on hand has expanded. It's just shy of $50 million, which gives us every day an opportunity to make a decision around share repurchases or ETH acquisitions. You would have seen in June when we raised the $75 million, we did both. We raised capital accretively.

We did some share repurchases, and we also bought ETH. So we have a team who's able to do that. We're not in a rush, and we're not here to accumulate ETH for the sake of accumulation. We're going to do things that make sense for our long-term investment thesis and grow ETH per share. That is how we think about it. It doesn't change in an upmarket or a down market. We have the flexibility, and that's the beauty of an Ethereum treasury strategy.

We are seeing a lot of inbounds, but we're going to be very careful and thoughtful to do financing when it makes sense, to do stock repurchases when it makes sense and to buy ETH when it's accretive for investors.

The airline’s newest lounge will be the second-largest in the network, offering flyers an upgraded experience at Dulles.

You’ll no longer have to go to the basement to get into a United Club at Washington Dulles International Airport.

The brand-new United Club in the new IAD Concourse E spans nearly 40,000 square feet across an upstairs floor and can seat 630 passengers, making it a significant upgrade to the carrier’s existing lounge portfolio at the airport. It’s the second-largest United Club after its newest lounge in Houston, which opened just weeks earlier.

The new lounge by gates E14 and E16 opens to customers Nov. 10, 2026. United invited me to a media preview of the lounge, and here’s what you can expect inside.

The lounge features several nods to D.C.’s iconic landmarks and monuments, as well as the region’s natural beauty.

When you first enter the lounge, you’ll need to scan your boarding pass and then head up the escalators (stairs and elevators are also available) to get to the lounge.

One of my favorite design features as a former D.C. resident is that escalator ride up, which has been recreated to feel like you’re inside a Metro station.

Thankfully, the escalator ride is not as long as at some stations. Looking at you, Dupont Circle!

Once you're upstairs, you’ll walk into the heart of the lounge, with two buffet stations, a centerpiece bar and plenty of seating options, whether you’re traveling as a group or by yourself. (More on food and beverage options later.)

It’s impossible to miss the soaring ceilings in this lounge, especially compared to the bunker-like atmosphere at some of the existing United Clubs.

Don’t forget to look up, where you’ll see a cherry blossom sculpture, an homage to one of the region’s most popular attractions.

There are also two additional lounging areas on both sides of the central area. One is inspired by the Blue Ridge Mountains, which you can see in the distance.

The other has a cherry blossom theme, with light fixtures that branch out from the ceiling.

Massive windows run throughout the lounge, allowing in tons of natural light and offering fantastic views of the airfield. United has a major presence at IAD, so expect to see plenty of United planes.

The United Club has a full kitchen, allowing it to offer upgraded food options compared to its existing lounges at IAD.

You can expect to find sandwiches, salads and hot protein dishes. The lounge also had a ramen bar and a chili bar set up during my visit.

The two buffet stations are located right next to each other, with a dessert station in between.

If you want something to drink, you can head to the bar or one of the hydration stations throughout the space.

There’s plenty of seating at the bar, which has a double archway design. There are also large TVs if you’re trying to keep up with one of Washington’s many sports teams.

The United Club has eight phone booths for those who need to make a call. They’re split between the two lounging areas in the club.

You'll also find a single-stall private restroom, a wellness room, and dedicated men’s and women’s restrooms.

There are no showers in this lounge. To access a shower in a United lounge, you’ll need to head to the Polaris Lounge, reserved exclusively for eligible business class passengers flying on United and select partner airlines.

You can access the United Club by holding elite status, a lounge membership, the right credit card or an eligible premium cabin ticket.

If there’s availability, United sells day passes at the door for flights departing within three hours. You’ll also need a valid same-day boarding pass on a United or Star Alliance flight.

Holding the right credit card is probably the easiest way to get in. United’s most high-end card comes with a United Club membership, while others might offer one-time passes.

If you’re looking for a United lounge, the newest club in Concourse E is where you want to be. It offers more space, lots of light and elevated food options compared to other United Clubs.

Its massive footprint could also ease overcrowding, a common complaint with other lounges.

One thing to consider is location. The concourses at IAD are spread out, and you may need to take a mobile lounge or train to get there. If you want to check out the lounge, make sure you give yourself enough time to get to your gate.

#3089. Monday.com: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Shifting upmarket trades near-term SMB churn for deeper enterprise ties, and Frontier's deploy engineers are the bet that makes it stick.

On its third-quarter fiscal year 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 9, 2026, monday.com (MNDY -9.10%) announced third-quarter revenue of $378 million, up 19% year over year. The enterprise software company is shifting its focus from small accounts to large enterprise clients while pairing artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities with human workflows. This corporate transition creates near-term sales friction but deepens long-term customer relationships. Three things management said stand out.

Management is intentionally directing sales resources toward larger corporate clients while reducing acquisition efforts for smaller buyers. Small and medium business (SMB) customer churn increased as a direct result of this strategy and recent workforce reductions.

The business is migrating clients to a hybrid pricing structure that combines standard seat subscriptions with usage-based credit packages. Annual recurring revenue (ARR), a metric measuring the annualized value of subscription contracts, reached $36 million from these AI capabilities.

Large corporate accounts require hands-on technical support to integrate software into existing operational workflows. Management created monday Frontier, a specialized service organization that embeds technical specialists into client operations to deploy tailored solutions.

Longer sales cycles and workforce cuts create operational friction, yet enterprise software adoption is deepening across large customer accounts. Proprietary software capabilities and dedicated deployment engineers provide structural momentum while management monitors pricing discipline and net dollar retention.

Scaling enterprise relationships and embedding artificial intelligence directly into daily operations remain central to driving long-term value.

#3088. Shopify Is Down 10% in 1 Month. Here's Why I'd Still Buy and Hold It for the Next Decade.

Shopify's dip hides a business that makes it hard for merchants to leave.

Shopify (SHOP +2.12%) shares are down about 10% over the last month, as of Nov. 5, after its latest quarterly results came in slightly below Wall Street's expectations. Investors shouldn't get caught up in Wall Street's expectations trap. The reason the stock is worth buying is that Shopify is still winning business from major brands, with an enormous opportunity still ahead.

Shopify's competitive edge is bringing stores, payments, inventory, and financing together on one platform for a subscription fee. This removes a lot of friction for merchants, and as merchants engage with different services, it makes Shopify hard to replace.

One service can open the door to a deeper business relationship. For example, Alice + Olivia decided to move its business onto the platform after starting with Shop Pay. Shopify continues to win over other brands, including Lululemon and Balmain, which went live on Shopify last quarter.

Its merchant lending business, Shopify Capital, creates another sticky relationship with merchants. In the third quarter, Shopify purchased about $1.5 billion of merchant loans and cash advances, up from $1 billion a year earlier. Financing introduces credit risk, but it gives merchants another reason to stay with Shopify, which is more important for long-term growth.

Overall, merchants sold $119 billion worth of goods, or gross merchandise volume (GMV), through Shopify in the third quarter, up 29% from a year earlier. That's almost as much as they sold on Shopify in all of 2020, when the pandemic pushed shopping online.

Shopify handled about $477 billion in annualized GMV in the third quarter, compared with eMarketer's estimate of more than $6 trillion in global e-commerce sales. That's a small share of less than 10%, though Shopify includes offline sales, so this is an approximate comparison. There is still substantial room to expand.

That runway is why investors have historically paid a high sales multiple for the stock. It trades around 14 times trailing sales as of Nov. 5, which is high but in line with its three-year average. And as Warren Buffett wrote in his 1989 shareholder letter, "It's far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price."

Shopify is a quality growth stock worth paying up for. Management expects revenue growth in the low 30% range in the fourth quarter, and with less than 10% of global e-commerce today, Shopify can sustain a high growth rate for many years. A business building sticky relationships with merchants and growing that fast is worth holding for the long term, even if it looks expensive today.

#3086. Texas Paused Data Center Permits Before the Election. Here's Why That Context Matters for AI Investors.

Government intervention in data center development could have broad implications for the market.

The market has been worried about artificial intelligence (AI) spending for months now, but the market has continued to climb, leaving some of the biggest spenders behind.

However, after last week's election, AI stocks have been dropping, pulling the S&P 500 lower. The market is worried that new legislation could hinder data center growth and, by default, slow down AI development.

Texas had already paused permits on data centers even before the elections, and Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has pledged to put a moratorium on building until the government could work with the people to see what their needs are.

While some AI stocks soared after the election results, the market was routed on Thursday as investors took in the implications of a new Congress.

The market did a 180 on Thursday after what appeared to be a positive reaction to the election results on Wednesday. At first, investors embraced the idea of a slowdown, as spend has put many top tech companies into a negative free cash flow zone.

Another way to look at is that companies that already have a robust platform are in a strong position against smaller rivals who still need to build out. That's why Amazon and Alphabet were rising on Wednesday before dropping again.

However, sentiment turned negative on Thursday as the market began to digest the broader implications of what new government could mean.

Texas's vast landscape has been the site of massive data center build-outs, and it accounts for 25% to 30% of planned capacity to be developed by 2030. In the first few months of 2026 alone, almost 200 data centers were asked to be added to the electric grid. About 90% of large energy consumers who have asked for massive amounts of energy -- five times the amount needed to power the entire state when there was record-breaking demand -- came from data centers.

Texas's current governor has already initiated an audit to assess how much energy is being used and how it affects residents' energy consumption and bills, but state lawmakers have questioned whether companies can be compelled to participate in an audit without a law being passed. The new state government under Hinojosa may pass the necessary laws to make it happen. "The only way we can have any assurances that the people will be protected is if there is a moratorium until the legislature can meet and pass into actual law real protections for people," she said.

The other two states at the center of AI development -- Georgia and Ohio -- also just elected new Democratic governors who plan to halt permits.

While Amazon and Alphabet may be developed enough to see results and improved cash flow, the "pick and shovel" plays like Nvidia and Broadcom could be highly affected by pauses in data center development. Their stocks fell 8% and 9%, respectively, in one day, while the S&P 500 fell more than 4%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq composite fell 5.5%.

Much of Nvidia's rapid growth story right now is dependent on the continued pace of data centers being built, for example. It has been reporting accelerating growth, including a doubling of revenue in the 2027 fiscal second quarter (ended July 26), but that rate will slow if build does. Many AI and AI-adjacent companies will be in this boat, and their stocks won't be worth as much if their growth rates decline.

The fact that the market didn't respond to Texas' original permit pause just means it didn't know how seriously lawmakers would take this. As new governments are swept into office with an agenda that could be critical of AI development, the AI bubble might pop.

#3084. Prediction Markets Are Arriving in Your Investing App, and That Makes Us Nervous

NerdWallet, Inc. is an independent publisher and comparison service, not an investment advisor. Its articles, interactive tools and other content are provided to you for free, as self-help tools and for informational purposes only. They are not intended to provide investment advice. NerdWallet does not and cannot guarantee the accuracy or applicability of any information in regard to your individual circumstances. Examples are hypothetical, and we encourage you to seek personalized advice from qualified professionals regarding specific investment issues. Our estimates are based on past market performance, and past performance is not a guarantee of future performance.

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. And while our site doesn’t feature every company or financial product available on the market, we’re proud that the guidance we offer, the information we provide and the tools we create are objective, independent, straightforward — and free.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us. This may influence which products we review and write about (and where those products appear on the site), but it in no way affects our recommendations or advice, which are grounded in thousands of hours of research. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews of their products or services. Here is a list of our partners.

Prediction markets are booming, but that doesn’t make them a sound investment strategy.

The investing information provided on this page is for educational purposes only. NerdWallet, Inc. does not offer advisory or brokerage services, nor does it recommend or advise investors to buy or sell particular stocks, securities or other investments.

Around this time every year, we conduct NerdWallet’s annual broker review process. We assess what’s changed in the industry, discuss which brokerage features matter most (and which ones now matter less), and finally, we do the work by opening accounts to test them.

Prediction markets, which have made their way into some of the most popular investing apps, came up more than we expected in testing this year.

At first, we decided to simply collect information on who does and doesn’t offer access to them, without intending to reward or penalize a broker either way. It would be a neutral presentation of facts, not something that would factor into how we scored a broker.

But one afternoon, all together in the office, we confronted an uncomfortable question: “Do prediction markets, and such easy access to them within an investment app, go against NerdWallet’s editorial house views?”

After careful consideration, we all agreed: they do.

So we started to configure our 2027 rubric with a firmer stance against this trendy feature, penalizing brokers that actively market sports and entertainment event contracts, and whose prediction markets come with few, if any, guardrails.

We’ve distilled our discussion down to three main points:

These products are being marketed alongside investments.

We fear they could be discouraging long-term investing.

Let’s start here: Many aspects of trading could be seen as gambling-adjacent. Options, futures, highly leveraged single-day equity bets and even crypto can all easily fall into the “highly speculative” category. So why are we picking on prediction markets in particular?

In our view, a key differentiator is a much lower barrier to entry with few in-app guardrails in place.

Most of the products we mentioned above require some level of fluency — and at times even permission from the broker — to dabble in. To trade options, for example, you need to answer questions about your investing proficiency, your finances and more. And even after approval, the terminology required to trade can be so intimidating that the language itself can become an indirect deterrent.

Event contracts, which form the backbone of prediction markets, are largely presented in the vernacular, and our testing showed approval to trade them is completed with a few taps from the home screen. Moreover, their content is often unrelated to finance — according to a May 2026 report by the Pew Research Center, around 80% of volume on the prediction market platform Kalshi was for sports events[1]Pew Research Center. Trading Volume on Prediction Markets Has Soared in Recent Months. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

Answering a binary question (yes/no; this/that), posed in everyday language about a familiar topic — something like, “Will the Knicks beat the Spurs on Sunday?” — can be far less daunting than figuring out what an options chain is or understanding forex pairs.

In other words, what makes prediction markets accessible to a wider audience is also what makes them problematic, especially when housed within an investing account. Which brings us to our next point.

On the platforms that feature them, we found that prediction markets almost always appear alongside stock and ETF trading. We think this is a mistake. What has made these mobile-first investing apps so good for so long (making it easy to move, manage and invest money through a beautiful interface) is what’s now making us nervous.

For example, most investing platforms let users do any number of smart things with idle cash. They could open an Individual Retirement Account (IRA), a custodial account or a robo-managed portfolio all through a single app. But now, they can dip into that same pot of money to bet on whether Beyoncé or Alicia Keys will play the Super Bowl halftime show.

But is anyone actually trading these event contracts? Let’s use data from publicly traded brokers that offer prediction markets to explore this.

In Q3 2026, Robinhood’s revenue from event contracts rose more than 600% year over year to $173 million, while the number of event contracts traded grew more than sevenfold to 16.4 billion[2]Robinhood. Robinhood Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources . This was the second-highest source of transaction revenue behind options trading. In a forecast reported on by Cointelegraph, Bernstein analysts projected Robinhood’s prediction markets could drive $1.7 billion in annual revenue by 2028[3]Yahoo Finance. Bernstein Sees Robinhood Prediction Markets Reaching $1.7 Billion in Revenue by 2028, Topping Crypto. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

Coinbase's Q1 2026 quarterly report called prediction markets “one of its fastest-scaling products ever, driven by strong retail interest[4]Coinbase. Coinbase Q1 Financial Results Show Resilient Financial Performance Driven by New All-Time High Crypto Trading Volume Market Share. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources ."

In a call discussing Webull’s Q2 results, U.S. CEO Anthony Denier noted trading volume in Webull’s nascent prediction market product grew about 70% quarter over quarter[5]Gloom. Webull (BULL) Q2 2026 earnings call transcript. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources .

Gemini’s Q2 report shows prediction market volume rose 93% quarter over quarter[6]Gemini. Shareholder Update Q2 2026. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

So, now that we’ve established that these markets are growing in popularity — and investing platforms appear to have a large incentive to lean into them — how are all those event contract traders faring? That brings us to our final point.

Is all this even worth it? Several studies show how hard it is to actually turn a profit in prediction markets. Here are a few:

One study, conducted by researchers at ESSEC Business School, HEC Montréal and the University of Toronto's Rotman School of Management, covered 2.4 million Polymarket accounts across $67 billion in trading volume between November 2022 and March 2026, and found that 69% of users lost money[7]SSRN. Who Wins and Who Loses In Prediction Markets? Evidence from Polymarket. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources . Moreover, the top 1% of users who made a profit accounted for about 76% of all gains. Translation: Even if you did turn a profit, there’s a good chance you didn’t make much.

A Bloomberg analysis supports this: From January 2025 to April 2026, more than 100,000 Polymarket accounts lost at least $1,000[8]Bloomberg. Most Prediction Market Traders Are Losing Money While Bots Rack Up Gains. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources . Of the 2 million active wallets studied, almost half made or lost less than $10 during the period, while far fewer accounts collected larger profits.

A separate Wall Street Journal analysis echoed the same trend: 67% of Polymarket profits go to 0.1% of accounts, and more than 70% of Polymarket users lost money[9]The Wall Street Journal. Why Almost Everyone Loses—Except a Few Sharks—on Prediction Markets. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources .

While there is far less data available on Kalshi trades (Polymarket runs on a public blockchain, making it easy to extract and analyze data), a Kalshi spokesperson confirmed in the Wall Street Journal analysis above that one month of data in 2026 showed there were 2.9 unprofitable users to each profitable user[10]Wall Street Journal. Why Almost Everyone Loses—Except a Few Sharks—on Prediction Markets. Accessed Nov 10, 2026. View all sources .

The first study above discusses how event contract trading is binary and zero-sum: If one trader wins, another loses. This means traders allocating money to these instruments could be missing out on aspects of equity markets that have helped create long-term wealth for previous generations.

“Unlike equity markets, there is no equity premium, no dividends, and no passive investment options. Their short maturities naturally encourage short-horizon trading, which is precisely what the behavioral finance literature has suggested is most destructive to wealth accumulation. Given the rapid growth of these platforms and their role as a potential entry point for young investors, understanding who bears the losses has direct implications for investor welfare and market regulation.”

As a reminder, the vast majority of Polymarket users bore the losses.

At NerdWallet, our mission has always been to help people make smarter financial decisions, so we’re sticking by that. Starting with our 2027 ratings, brokers that offer easy access to sports and entertainment event contracts will lose points in our scoring system because we believe this new product has the potential to harm long-term wealth building and doesn’t belong in investing platforms.

So, what’s a better way forward? Bring back the friction and make prediction markets a separate app. Financial institutions, businesses and individuals can still explore legitimate use cases for prediction markets, such as forecasting and hedging. And we’re not here to stop anyone from trading event contracts for entertainment with extra money. We just don’t want these markets so easily conflated with the legitimate investing vehicles these apps already offer. And our reviews will reflect that.

Mark Stolper: Thanks, Kees. I'm now going to briefly review our third quarter performance and attempt to highlight what I believe to be some material items. I will also provide an update to 2026 financial guidance levels, which were amended in conjunction with last evening's financial results press release. In my discussion, I will use the term adjusted EBITDA, which is a non-GAAP financial measure.

The company defines adjusted EBITDA as earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization and excludes losses or gains on the disposal of equipment, other income or loss, loss on debt extinguishments and noncash equity compensation. Adjusted EBITDA includes equity and earnings of unconsolidated operations and subtracts allocations of earnings to noncontrolling interest in subsidiaries and is adjusted for noncash or extraordinary and onetime events taking place during the period. A full quantitative reconciliation of adjusted EBITDA to net income or loss attributable to RadNet, Inc. common shareholders is included in the earnings release. I will also be using a second non-GAAP measure pertaining to the Digital Health segment called annual recurring revenue, or ARR.

We use ARR as a key operating metric to evaluate the scale, growth and health of the recurring component of our digital health business. We define ARR as a key subscription economy metric, representing the predictable normalized annualized value of contracted recurring revenue generated from active customer contracts. ARR includes subscription fees, recurring support fees and contracted usage charges and excludes onetime or nonrecurring fees such as implementation fees, hardware sales, professional services, consulting and onetime training. ARR is determined based on the contractual terms of active customer arrangements and is not calculated by reference to revenue recognized under GAAP, deferred revenue or another GAAP financial measure.

ARR is not a forecast of future revenue, which may be affected by contract start and end dates, cancellations, renewal rates, customer usage and other factors. With that said, I'd now like to review our third quarter results. While I won't recap all the financial information that's contained in last night's earnings report, here are some highlights. Revenue increased 22.1% and adjusted EBITDA increased 23.8% as compared with last year's third quarter.
